question: Infrasound is sound with a frequency below the lower limit of human hearing. Widely occurring in nature (for example, in earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, etc.), it is also artificially generated by wind turbines. Since infrasound propagates over vast distances with virtually no losses, it can affect the whole body, disrupting cellular processes in humans and animals. As a result, it can also be used as a weapon.

1 A recent study from the infrasound working group at the Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz found that areas where wind energy has expanded massively are experiencing a markedly higher rate of newly diagnosed cardiovascular disease (heart arrhythmias, cardiac insufficiency).

2Infrasound can cause balance disturbances, dizziness, nausea, sleep disorders, changes to blood flow, an increase in blood pressure, and damage to lungs and internal organs. There can also be adverse psychological effects, particularly reduced concentration.
3 In the meantime, three judgments have been handed down by courts in Belgium and France4, awarding local residents compensation for wind-turbine-induced health problems.5 1.
Why has it trivialised the dangers associated with wind turbines up to now, and how will it make people aware of these dangers in future?
What is its view of the court judgments from Belgium and France acknowledging health problems caused by wind turbines?
